messages:
jessica_l: Noticed a weird uptick in fncall.validation.rejects in ap-southeast. ~2.5% in 30m, mostly unknown_union_member errors.

mark_s: Any clues? sample: 
```json
{
  "response": { "type": "ChoiceA", "payload": { "v": 1 } },
  "extras": null
}
expected union: ChoiceA | ChoiceB | {Fallback}
```

anita_p: That's likely from the recent union-appliance change that enforces explicit discriminators. Did we flip on discriminator_required=true in ap-southeast?

ops-bot: deploy: validator/union-discriminator updated to 100% in ap-southeast by @ops. Commit: c1b2d3.

jessica_l: That was supposed to be 25% canary. Similar rollout templating bug again.

mark_s: Mitigation options: 1) enable union_compat_mode=true which treats unknown members as Fallback, incrementing fncall.union_fallbacks_total; 2) revert rollout to 25%; 3) create an alert for >0.3% absolute jump in union rejects over 5m.

anita_p: I vote for (1)+(2). Keep signal via metric but avoid spikes. Also add a transient field in the validator logs to capture offending discriminator values for follow-up.

jessica_l: I'll rollback to 25% and flip union_compat_mode=true. Adding PromQL: 
```
sum by(region) (rate(fncall_union_rejects_total[5m]))
sum by(region) (rate(fncall_union_fallbacks_total[5m]))
```

mark_s: Add panel showing top discriminator values using `topk(10, sum by(discriminator) (increase(fncall_union_reject_values_total[5m])))` — that will require adding label capture in the metric.

ops-bot: action: rollback validator/union-discriminator -> target_percentage=25% by @jessica_l.

jessica_l: Done. union_compat_mode=true set in `/config/validators/fncall/ap-southeast.json`. Added log field capture.

anita_p: I'll open a docs PR to call out discriminator behavior and backwards-compatible approaches.

jessica_l: TL;DR: accidental full rollout for discriminator enforcement; rolled back to 25%; enabled compat fallback; added dashboards, alert, and telemetry to capture offending discriminator values.

mark_s: Nice. We'll watch for the rejects to fall under 0.2% in 10m. :ok_hand:
